subject: general
question: Find the area of a triangle whose sides are of lengths 5 cm, 12 cm and 13 cm.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **Pythagorean triplet**: 5, 12, 13 satisfy 5² + 12² = 13² (25 + 144 = 169).

Since it is a **right-angled triangle**, Area = 1/2 × base × height.

Area = 1/2 × 5 × 12 = 30 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 30 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sides **a** = 5 cm, **b** = 12 cm, **c** = 13 cm.

**Formula Used:** Heron's Formula → Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)], where s = (a+b+c)/2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2282e4ab6fb064afe17afb8b48c4db73f685bc13179b4e82bc692e6f21a21178.png] 

⇒ Semi-perimeter (s) = (5 + 12 + 13) ÷ 2

⇒ s = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm

⇒ Area = √[15 × (15 − 5) × (15 − 12) × (15 − 13)]

⇒ Area = √[15 × 10 × 3 × 2]

⇒ Area = √900

⇒ Area = 30 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 30 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Triplets

Common sets of three positive integers that satisfy **a² + b² = c²** include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25).

Area of Equilateral Triangle

For a triangle with all sides equal to 'a', Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × a².

Right-Angled Triangle Property

The area is always half the product of the two sides forming the 90-degree angle (base and altitude).</p
